story.title: Arrests Made in Homicide of Mississippi Woman Found Hanging in Staged Scene
story.summary: Authorities have arrested a third suspect in the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old woman found hanging from a tree behind an abandoned home in Jackson, Mississippi, in August. Police have ruled her death a homicide, stating that the scene was staged following a drug dispute. The exact cause of her death has not been disclosed.

event_overview.title: About Mississippi Homicide
event_overview.subject: Mississippi Homicide
event_overview.summary: This is the homicide investigation into the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old woman whose body was found hanging from a tree behind a vacant home in west Jackson, Mississippi, on August 3, 2026. Authorities later classified the death as a homicide; investigators testified that they believe the hanging occurred after her death, while the precise cause of death had not been publicly disclosed as of September 26, 2026.

facts.label: Discovery and location
facts.value: Fortune was found on August 3, 2026, in the backyard of a vacant home in west Jackson, including reporting that placed the site in the 500 block of Road of Remembrance.

facts.label: Investigating authority
facts.value: The Jackson Police Department is the lead local agency publicly reporting on the case; Chief RaShall Brackney said the state medical examiner's office determined that Fortune's death was a homicide on September 10, 2026.

facts.label: Nature of the allegation
facts.value: At a September 25 court hearing, a Jackson police detective testified, citing the medical examiner's opinion, that Fortune was already dead when her body was hanged and that the scene was staged. That testimony was part of an ongoing criminal case, not a final judicial finding.

facts.label: Criminal proceedings
facts.value: By September 25, authorities had announced murder charges against multiple men; the first defendant, Jarques Ratliff, had pleaded not guilty and was awaiting continuation of a preliminary hearing set for September 30 to determine whether sufficient evidence existed to send the matter to a grand jury.

event_overview.scope_note: This timeline follows key publicly reported developments in the investigation and arrests connected to Fortune's death, but does not purport to cover every filing, hearing, investigative lead, or any final adjudication.

explore_lenses.label: Why does the staged-scene finding matter?
explore_lenses.title: It changes the central investigative question
explore_lenses.summary: The medical examiner’s homicide finding and a detective’s testimony that the hanging was staged shift the case from an apparent hanging to an alleged killing followed by concealment or misdirection. That distinction explains why investigators have pursued multiple murder charges while withholding some forensic details.

claims.text: At a September 25 preliminary hearing, Jackson Police Detective Samuel Dukes testified, citing the medical examiner’s opinion, that Fortune’s hanging was staged; he also said investigators believed she may have been killed elsewhere.
The exact cause of Fortune’s death has not been publicly released, so “staged” does not yet establish the precise mechanism of killing or each defendant’s alleged role.
Because the public discovery scene recalled historic lynchings, the staged-scene allegation is especially consequential; authorities have not publicly said that race was a motive.

explore_lenses.label: What evidence links the case to a drug dispute?
explore_lenses.title: The theory is testimony, not a public final account
explore_lenses.summary: Police have presented a preliminary theory that Fortune was killed after a dispute involving drugs, but the detective did not disclose the underlying evidence in open court because the investigation and grand-jury process are incomplete. The defense disputes the first defendant’s involvement.

claims.text: Detective Dukes testified that the apparent motive was a disagreement over drugs and that interviews indicated Fortune fought hard before she was killed.
Dukes declined to give additional details at the hearing because the grand jury had not received all evidence, leaving the factual basis for the alleged drug dispute undisclosed publicly.
Jarques Ratliff has pleaded not guilty; his attorney, Toney Baldwin, said Ratliff denies involvement and that he wants the truth to emerge.

explore_lenses.label: What happens after the third arrest?
explore_lenses.title: Three murder cases and a continuing investigation
explore_lenses.summary: As of September 26, Eric Clark had become the third person charged with murder after turning himself in; police say the investigation remains active. Ratliff’s preliminary hearing was set to resume September 30, a proceeding focused on probable cause rather than guilt.

claims.text: Jackson police said Eric Clark, 45, turned himself in on September 25 and was charged with murder, joining Jarques Ratliff, 51, and Earnest Lloyd Jr., 25, as people charged in Fortune’s death.

Ratliff’s preliminary hearing was scheduled to resume on September 30; Mississippi preliminary hearings test probable cause and, if probable cause is found, the case is bound over for grand-jury action.
Police said additional warrants were expected before Clark’s arrest, and the department still describes the investigation as ongoing; further arrests remain possible but are not confirmed.

story_report.summary: Jackson police have charged three people with murder in the death of Tasia Fortune, who was found hanging from a tree in August. Police have ruled her death a homicide and say the scene was staged after what investigators describe as a drug-related dispute. Eric Clark, 45, turned himself in on September 25, joining Jarques Ratliff, 51, and Earnest Lloyd Jr., 25, among those charged. The investigation remains ongoing, while Ratliff’s preliminary hearing was set to resume September 30.

sections.heading: Staged Scene Raises Public Questions
sections.body: At Ratliff’s September 25 preliminary hearing, Jackson Police Detective Samuel Dukes testified that, citing the medical examiner’s opinion, Fortune’s hanging had been staged. Dukes said investigators believed she may have been killed elsewhere. Because the public discovery scene recalled historic lynchings, the allegation carries particular weight, though authorities have not publicly said race was a motive.

sections.heading: Drug Dispute Claim Faces Denial
sections.body: Dukes testified that investigators believed a disagreement over drugs was the apparent motive and that interviews indicated Fortune fought hard before she was killed. He declined to provide additional details because the grand jury had not received all the evidence. Ratliff has pleaded not guilty; his attorney, Toney Baldwin, said Ratliff denies involvement and wants the truth to emerge.

sections.heading: Charges Move Toward Grand Jury
sections.body: In Mississippi, a preliminary hearing assesses whether probable cause exists; if it does, the case is bound over for grand-jury action. Police had said additional warrants were expected before Clark’s arrest and continue to describe the investigation as ongoing. Further arrests are possible, but none have been confirmed.

unresolved.text: The exact cause of Fortune’s death, the full autopsy findings and the alleged sequence of events have not been publicly released.
Publicly available material does not identify the drugs involved, detail the alleged dispute, establish who initiated it, or say whether prosecutors will allege a racial motive.
It remains unclear whether all three defendants will be indicted, whether they would be tried together or separately, and whether anyone else will face charges.

related_stories.title: Severe Flooding in Bangkok Leads to Disaster Declaration
related_stories.summary: Heavy rainfall over the past few days has resulted in significant flooding across Bangkok, prompting officials to declare a state of disaster in all 50 districts of the city. Reports indicate that some areas received more than 30 centimeters (12 inches) of rain within 48 hours, leading to widespread inundation and submerged roads.
